reason: Product direction and demand validation directly match assessing product ideas.
A read-only onboarding friction audit directly matches UX improvement work.
A user-facing checkout feature requires usability and reliable execution judgment.
Scoped dashboard clarity and visual improvements directly match improving user-facing products.
Planning an activation test directly addresses adoption problems.
Translation without meaning changes is copy-only work, explicitly outside scope.
An import-path fix is unrelated debugging and explicitly excludes product review.
A behavior-preserving variable rename is a mechanical refactor.
Shortening an email without evaluating its offer is copy-only work.
Explaining algorithmic complexity does not require product judgment.
Alphabetizing JSON keys is mechanical work regardless of the product name.
An internal batch-job retry is unrelated to user-facing product improvement.
